articleTitle: Multidimensional digital signal processing for high definition television
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Summary form only given: Digital signal processing fundamentals for multidimensional systems (such as television) are reviewed. An appropriate signal decomposition for transmission and reconstruction for display is described employing both spatial and temporal signal processing. This leads to a choice of resolution and picture quality achievable at the expense of hardware complexity. The artifacts introduced by interlaced transmission to conserve transmission bandwidth can be substantially reduced by sequential scanning at both the source and display. Solutions for removing display artifacts are given. The requirements for artifact free motion portrayal are shown. Several adaptive processing algorithms are analyzed. The complexity required for various system implementations is examined. The practical realization of several key components impacting the receiver design is discussed. Conclusions and recommendations for future research are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CMOS 8-bit 20MHz two-step parallel A/D converter with 95mW power consumption
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The need for a low-cost, high-speed A/D converter with low power consumption is growing as digital video-signal processing applications in the consumer electronics field increase. Although a flash ADC offers a sufficiently high conversion rate for video applications, it has a high power consumption because of its large number of comparators. The two-step parallel ADC, on the other hand, has significantly fewer comparators, and thus a lower power consumption and, because its chip size is smaller, it can be made at lower cost. A conventional two-step parallel ADC has, however, three problems: a relatively slow conversion rate, a relatively poor differential linearity, and the need for a peripheral sample-and-hold circuit. The authors report a new 8-bit two-step parallel ADC which solves these problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CD-ROM assisted navigation system
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A path-induction navigation system with aural direction has been developed by using CD-ROM and aural information for versatile and safer navigation. CD-ROM ensures high-precision self-sustained navigation and provides multiple mobile information. In the several years since its first implementation, the mobile navigation system has been the core of mobile information system. The heart of system is a database containing information that does not change, stored on CD-ROM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The benefits of a progressive scan based HDTV system
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The introduction of High Definition Television (HDTV) as the new high quality television system for the future must avoid all deficiencies of today's systems. In addition, the pictures must be of noticeably higher quality than todays. On the other hand, consumer equipment must not be so expensive that a successful introduction will be hindered. The proposed progressive scan based system fulfils the requirements of the CCIR (twice the resolution in both spatial dimensions, good motion rendition) and allows for economic production of consumer equipment. In addition, the choice of parameters allows for future improvements in terms of spatial resolution and full digital transmission.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of RF channels for television systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Television FM and VSB-AM processes, including channel impairments, have been implemented in software on an image-processing computer system. By interfacing RF channel programs with baseband programs, complex systems can be evaluated in an expeditious, controlled, repeatable manner.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital video signal processing system in home VCRs
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The newly developed digital video signal processing system in home VCRs with the luminance signal digitized by a clock signal locked to horizontal sync and the chrominance signal digitized by a burst locked clock and converted to color difference signal is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power concept for HDTV
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: HDTV will require circuits working at 31 kHz, 45 kHz or perhaps even 62.5 kHz. The consequences of the choice are analyzed. The paper also reviews the line deflection circuit and the power supply, using a new didactic method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Princeton Engine: a real-time video system simulator
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The Princeton Engine is a 29.3 GIPS image processing system capable of simulating video rate signals-including NTSC and HDTV video-in real-time. It consists of a massively-parallel arrangement of up to 2048 processing elements. Each processing element contains a 16-bit arithmetic unit, multiplier, a 64-word triple-port register stack (one write, two read), and 16000 words of local processor memory. In addition, an interprocessor communication bus (IPC) permits exchanges of data between neighboring processors during one instruction cycle. The authors describe a new, graphical, method of parallel programming for DSP applications and provide several examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The full digital video camera system and simulation of its essential parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Describes a full digital video camera system. Advanced computer control methods and its essential parameters that are drawn out from the computer simulation, and well compromised to various demands in the consumer electronics field are described. The main stream of video signal processing used in consumer video cameras has been built up with an analogue signal processing technique. However, since some high quality picture formats are spreading, an investigation to improve picture quality by means of a digital signal processing technique is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alignment free digital videorecorder-servo concept
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A new alignment-free servo concept for a VHS recorder uses a microprocessor for digital regulation in combination with a new drum-motor control concept. The problem was how to reduce production costs and get a higher precision for the necessary adjustments. The solution is to let the servo controller to the critical and time intensive adjustments by itself.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DSP type coherent DSB signal detector using new phase synchronizer
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A digital signal processing (DSP) type coherent DSB (double side band) signal detector using new phase synchronizer is proposed. Computer simulation shows that the proposed system is well matched with the theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integral delayed and differential noise suppression method for CCD camera
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A new noise suppression method, the integral delayed and differential noise suppression (IDDS) method, has been developed. This is so effective not only in noise suppression but also in compensation for defective pixels that high picture quality can be obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compatible wide aspect ratio TV
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Describes a new proposal of wide aspect ratio TV signal format, which is fully compatible with current NTSC receivers and terrestrial transmitters. In order to realize the compatibility, the proposed signal features a new format of three dimensional frequency domain multiplexing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dual, single sideband: a crosstalk-resistant alternative to quadrature modulation with applications in ACTV
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Modulating signals on the upper and lower sidebands of a carrier has significant advantages over standard quadrature modulation in ACTV. Three dimensional Fourier analysis shows the carrier's placement in the 'Fukinuki' hole, as well its single-sideband nature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sub-Nyquist sampling of NTSC video
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: For deghosting purposes, both the in-phase and quadrature parts of the vestigial sideband TV signal are needed. This new scheme can reduce the sampling rate to lower than the Nyquist rate of either part. It comprises sampling rate reduction and complex signal processing for signal recovery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stereoscopic video movie camera '3D-CAM'
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: With mounting public interest, stereoscopic images are evolving from the domain of industrial and medical applications to come closer to us in the form of VHD video disks, electronic games. The authors have developed a stereoscopic video movie camera '3D-CAM', capable of shooting, recording, and reproducing stereoscopic images. This paper deals with the configurations and features of this camera and display units.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MUSE decoder
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A new MUSE decoder, for the reception of the HDTV broadcast signal, has been developed. This MUSE decoder, utilizing accurate motion detection, new interpolation method and refined nonlinear deemphasis, reproduces high quality HDTV pictures. Using this decoder, the feasibility of HDTV broadcasting by the MUSE system has been verified through a number of transmission tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A home bus system based on main bus and power line spread-spectrum bus
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Introduces a home bus system based on the Japanese standard. Through a combination of main bus and spread-spectrum power line bus, a highly reliable, high-speed, low-cost and flexible home bus system is realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interactive home shopping: the format of the future?
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: In the never ending pursuit of convenience, and the 'best bargain', a number of home shopping services have been developed. These delivery services include mail order catalogs, television programs, dedicated cable channels, and supported videotapes, videologs, and radio shows. A number of interactive shopping services have also appeared such as online computer services, videotext, and more recently two-way hybrid telecommunication prototypes such as J.C. Penny's Telaction and GTE's Main Street project. In the future, this line-up may be expanded to include any of a number of next-generation interactive home consumer systems such as CDI (compact disc interactive), DVI (digital video interactive), interactive videotape and broadband fiber optic services. Is interactive shopping the wave of the future?.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fully auto-adaptive microcontroller monitor
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Using a microcontroller improves the utilization and performance of this monitor which copes with any CRT adaptor card, recognizes the video mode, and sets all picture parameters defined by the user. The monitor must be able to adapt itself to different signal sources from various types and also work with a wide range of screen resolutions. Many solutions already exist which adapt each stage of the monitor independently. The author describes a central control system which measures signal parameters and sets up all stages of the monitor at the same time. The microcontroller and its connection with all stages is the real nerve center of the monitor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The stereoscopic field of pseudo-stereoscopic TV
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Offers a new idea called stereoscopic field of pseudo-stereoscopic TV. The author evaluates the advantages and shortcomings of the existing techniques and suggests four criteria which should be fulfilled by acceptable pseudotype TV. He then introduces some progress made in China.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced videotex terminal
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: An advanced videotex terminal which can display natural still-images with high speed using discrete cosine transform-vector quantization compression technology has been developed. In addition, it has an ADPCM voice and adapts to a digital network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new timing generator IC for a CCD imager
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Presents a timing generator IC for a high-resolution 768 H*492 V pixels CCD imager. As the output pulses of the IC are generated by an on-chip ROM, their timing can be changed with ease by reprogramming. The IC has been miniaturized to a very small quad flat package by utilizing the ROM. The authors show a peripheral block diagram of the timing generator IC, operation is synchronized by signals from an external sync generator IC. The timing generator IC generates clock pulses for the CCD imager and sampling pulses for the CCD output signal. The authors also show the block diagram of the IC which uniquely includes phase adjustment inverters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A family of surface acoustic wave filter for direct broadcasting satellite receiver
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The design, fabrication, performance and application of a family of SAW filters with center frequencies from 5.7 to 400 MHz and bandwidth from 1.3 to 27 MHz for DBS receivers are described. The quality assurance system, reliability test methods and failure analysis in batch production are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Consumer products designed and manufactured using FRESDAM
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The FRESDAM system, which can design three-dimensional freeform shapes and generate collision-free tool paths, is described and three FRESDAM-designed consumer products (headphones, a telephone receiver and a microphone) are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new custom-made IC for monitors
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The system evolution in the monitor field leads to the development of suitable ICs with performances and characteristics which are mainly monitor oriented rather than TV oriented. The automatic frequency raster preset of the monitors in computerised and optical equipment leads to the adoption of digital to analog converters in order to set the different parameters, and consequently all the regulations must be DC compatible. High scanning frequency and low jitter are additional factors that characterize the quality and the resolution of the monitors. New circuit solutions on silicon, concerning the monitor field, are described. In a single IC, the use of TTL compatible synchro pulses, horizontal and vertical processing functions and vertical ramp generation are implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trends in fiber for cable (TV)
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The cable industry has been relatively slow to adopt optical fiber as a major element of its networks. This arises in part because coaxial cable has suited cable's needs relatively well. Also, cable's basic task of delivering scores of video signals has posed some difficult economic and technical challenges for fiber technology. Fiber optic transmission offers the promise of significant benefit to the cable industry and it is important that one explores this potential and its relationship to consumer electronics issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The color reproduction technology for color video printer
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A high quality color video printer which employs a color reproduction LSI to produce prints of high quality approaching that of photographs has been developed for home use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cable's role in the development of HDTV systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: High definition television (HDTV) will be available within the USA by the early 1990's. At the same time, penetration of CATV has passed the 50% mark with no end in sight. All broadcast media including terrestrial broadcasters, cable operators, DBS and telco are formulating plans on how to best accommodate HDTV in their environments. Within the cable industry, the NCTA has focused on support of the FCC and ATSC in providing cable system testing. At American Television and Communications (ATC) and Home Box Office (HBO) efforts are being made to encourage the development of HDTV systems that are optimized for CATV carriage. A cable aware HDTV system must take into account existing practices within the cable industry including satellite delivery, interconnect systems, scrambling and security concepts, in addition to the basic coax system and its inherent signal transmission characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new tuning and display monochip for radio bands emitters and receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The T. Tuning Computer is a CMOS microcontroller including programmable LCD drivers, a new CMOS PLL concept and I/Os. This PLL integrates high speed prescaler (up to 250 MHz), reference frequency generator, phase comparator, programmable charge pumps and high voltage outputs for tuning. The chip is available in EPROM and ROM versions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cryptovision, a PAL video scrambler
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Describes a PAL video scrambling system based on a modification of the active line rotation principle. The scrambling method does not modify the synchronization signals and can therefore be used with any standard broadcasting system. It does not degrade the signal quality due to the scrambling and descrambling process. It gives very good scrambling and hence high security against unauthorized descrambling. It can easily be modified to work with NTSC signals. Subscriber decoders are in volume production.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transceiver controller IC for home bus system
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A transceiver controller IC has been developed for the improvement of the home bus system (HBS). The functions of the new IC cover the logical conditions of the physical layer of the OSI (open systems interconnection) reference model. Therefore, even a low cost, single chip microcomputer can easily control both home electronic products and the communication of HBS simultaneously by using the IC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprogrammable interface LSI on advanced domestic digital bus (ADDB)
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: In order to realize effective home automation, the correlative information network of home equipment is proposed. In this situation, the advanced domestic digital bus (ADDB) defined as the AV subsystem of a home bus system has arisen as the standard protocol internationally. The main features of ADDB are: multimaster communication; and transparent multimode system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The counting of received pixels in TV receiving systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Comparison of different HDTV transmission systems is very difficult. Main reason is that up till now these systems have not been available side by side for subjective tests on critical scenes. Objective criteria that determine the picture quality of a system have not been found yet. One could state that a calculation of the number of transmitted pixels is probably a rather bad way to determine the-subjective-quality of a transmission system. This quality will for instance also be determined by motion artifacts, flickering, aliasing etc. Nevertheless, counting the number of pixels might be the only 'comparison on paper' that is possible. That is why-be it with some hesitations-an attempt has been made to compare the number of received luminance pixels in NTSC, PAL, MAC, MUSE and HD-MAC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low noise one chip playback record head amplifier for VCR
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The design of a high performance play-back and record processor for VCR is described. The system architecture and the main performances are presented. The integrated circuit presented hereby contains all the functions necessary for the playback and the recording VCR processing. It is intended to be used for three heads applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low cost and flexible HCMOS microcomputer
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A modular approach is discussed which is based on a low cost 8 bit MCU core in 1.5 mu H-CMOS technology surrounded by a combination of megacell blocks. This meets application specific requirements for the large volume markets, like consumers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Consumer electronics bus, a robust communications system
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The Electronic Industries Association (EIA) is completing its consumer electronics bus (CEBus) standard to establish a common communication network through which any consumer electronics devices may exchange control information and data. The authors present some of the unique problems and solutions encountered by the committee in designing the CEBus protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-function communication terminal for home information services
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A multifunction communication terminal (MFT) which can perform such functions as videotex, teletext, PC communication, mail, and so on has been developed. A book type wireless remote controller was developed for efficient utilization of these functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Do consumers want interactive TV?
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Although it is impossible to predict consumer's response to interactive television, it may be possible to extract from current media usage patterns and attitudes some indications of how consumers may respond to interactive television in the future. A survey study was conducted at MIT's Audience Research Facility which: (1) examined the relationship between current media use and preferences for interactive television, (2) examined demographic and motivational differences in active and passive media use, and (3) explored audience response to various types of interactive television content and control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Alignment free mu P controlled CD servo concept
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: New CD servo concept with mu P adjustments for gains, offsets and detection levels. These adjustments can be permanently controlled and corrected during play-mode. As a result, the whole servo system works under optimum conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhanced NTSC system, free of chroma-crawl with improved resolution and cross chrominans
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Discusses two television systems developed by HRS which are fully compatible with NTSC and which eliminate chroma crawl and significantly reduce chrominance interference and moire.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of the power line carrier communications environment of the American home
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The growing interest in user installable home automation has prompted a considerable interest in the use of the AC power line for intrahome communications. The author describes an approach to characterize the ability of all types of American homes to support this power line carrier (PLC) communication. The effort described involves a considerable amount of field data acquisition, data reduction and extensive characterization of commonly found power line operated devices. The general approach chosen, the type of measurements made, and the type of information being distilled from the field data is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low-cost dual 16-bit DAC for digital audio equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Describes a dual 16-bit DAC which has THD of -75 dB and a dynamic range of 95 dB. It uses the symmetrical offset principle to achieve a (THD+noise)/S curve which closely approaches the ideal for small signals. No external components or adjustments are required. This integrated dual 16-bit digital DAC can be for use in audio equipment such a CD players and digital tape recorders. The flexible format for the input data allows simple interfacing with signal processing ICs such as interpolation filters, error correction circuits and audio signal processors. The high input bit-rate and fast-settling output facilitate application of the converter, together with simple external active analog filters (low-order, linear-phase filters), in oversampling systems. An adjustable current is added to the output currents to bias the external op-amps for maximum dynamic range. The converter is fabricated in a standard bipolar process, occupies a chip area of 3.5*3.1 mm/sup 2/ and comes in an 8-pin DIL package.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of an audio signal processor system based on DSP
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Describes the design of an audio signal processor system using a digital signal processor (DSP). The use of a high speed DSP with 24-bit wide data buses allows the implementation of many digital audio algorithms. These algorithms cover standard audio functions: equalizer, volume and balance control, as well as special functions: reverberations, base width enhancement, adaptive equalizer, dynamic range control, etc. The special audio functions are only available through the use of digital signal processing routines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of sequential and interlaced scan for HDTV with regard to spatial and temporal resolution
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The advantages of sequential over interlaced scan for any type of digital processing are well known but its penalty is the doubled bandwidth. A sequential 4-channel camera, which avoids this penalty, is presented and the three camera types-interlaced, sequential, 4-channel-are compared with regard to temporal and spatial resolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structural evaluation of a new 35" color TV plastic cabinet
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The attempt to adopt plastic cabinetry to 35" V color TV has been realized in order to achieve a lighter weight and a smaller footprint TV set. This paper presents the results of analyses and experiments undertaken for assuring the required strength of the newly developed plastic cabinet.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of multiple technology sources for consumer application VLSI design
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A common, technology-independent and easy-to-use design and layout system is presented. This CAD-system allows the implementation of different technologies from different semiconductor suppliers in a common manner. Thus, specific knowledge of detailed technology information is not necessary for the designer and layouter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive differential entropy-a new approach to high fidelity audio digital data rate reduction
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: New audio digital data rate reduction techniques, requiring under 10 percent of the computational burden of ADPCM that achieve near 16-bit CD fidelity with 4 to 6 bits per compressed sample, are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cableready television sets-the myth continues
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Cableready television sets are a three win situation: First, the consumer wins because features purchased with the television are not diminished by the presence of a cable converter; secondly, the cable operator wins because capital and operating maintenance costs are eliminated by not having to provide a converter; thirdly, the television manufacturer wins because more high end full feature television sets will be purchased. To be truly cableready, some rather stringent cable requirements must be met. Until those requirements are met, cableready television sets will remain a myth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tuner and demodulator performance for cable distributed D2-MAC TV-signals
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A system study on cable distribution of D2-MAC TV-signals has been carried out. With bit error rate as a D2-data performance parameter and visibility of disturbing signals as a performance reference for MAC-video components, system requirements are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A smearfree accordion CCD imager
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: A modified accordion clocking system offers an on-chip electronic method for the elimination of smear. The method is insensitive to spot movement. For frame transfer CCD imagers the clocking system provides an electronic shutter function as well. The smear suppression is also applicable to interline CCD imagers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A five-sample digital FM-demodulator with application to multichannel TV sound
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: In the FM receiver we shall sample the input signal at a rate F = 4f/(2N+1) = sample rate, where f is close to the carrier frequency. Five successive samples a,b,c,d,e are delivered to an arithmetic unit executing a particular algorithm that the authors define. The parameter D in the algorithm is a very good approximation of the frequency deviation d. In fact, if the input signal is a sinewave with a frequency f+d, then D is strictly a function of d. A carrier FM-modulated by a low frequency sinewave with d < F/20, has harmonic distortion < 0.5%. Thus the algorithm interprets the five samples as if they were samples of a sinewave. An analysis predicts that the behavior of the demodulator is in all respects very similar to analog demodulators with limiters, e.g. quadrature detectors. Random and quantization nOise in the input yield a "triangular" output noise spectrum. Together with oversampling, this effect allows for rough quantization of the input. A practical problem with this demodulator is that a nonlinear a/d converter may cause beats. The main problem, however, is arithmetic: the need for a division with the square of the carrier envelope puts a round-off error limit to the dynamic range. However, this is of no concern if the carrier has a fairly constant amplitude, such as the SAP subcarrier in the composite BTSC signal.

articleTitle: A TV-PLL-circuit for automatic tuner alignment
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Modern highly integrated TV systems are MCU controlled (12C-bus) and replace mechanical adjustment by electronic alignment. The integrated circuit described has been developed for such a system. The IC contains all PLL functions that are required to control a TV local oscillator and also includes a D to A converter section that generates three further varicap voltages for optimum control of the tuner filters. The unique feature of the IC is that it generates the four varactor control voltages on chip in a range of up to 30 V and that it also contains the PLL functions that require high frequency operation (1.3 GHz).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PAL encoding and decoding with improved luminance/chrominance separation
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: The application of digital signal processing techniques in TV receiver sets gives lots of improvements for picture quality. Images, which are free of disturbing flicker effects and which have reduced noise figures, can be achieved by adequate procedures, implemented at the home receiver. Also, image resolution can be increased and the appearance of crosstalk effects can be widely reduced, if comb filters are used to separate luminance and chrominance signals. But, dependent on filter characteristics and picture content, always some residual cross colour and cross luminance disturbances will remain even with comb filter decoding. This is due to the fact, that-already within the PAL encoding process-luminance and chrominance frequency components may exchange their assigned locations or even may share the same positions to give complete spectral overlap.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Consumer applications for 3D image synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: Applications for real time 3D image synthesis in consumer products are discussed. User interface and application structure issues are described with reference to a research application package, a kitchen designer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synchronous phase-reset FM carrier recording for reference bursts
publicationTitle: IEEE 1988 International Conference on Consumer Electronics Digest of Technical Papers.
abstract: In general, since the bandwidth of the video signal reproduced by home video cassette tape recorders (VCRs) is narrow below 2 MHz the burst signal cannot be directly recorded in the same way as the processing in the direct-FM recording VTR for broadcasting stations. But the NTSC signal whose chrominance signal is recorded by down-converted AM recording, can be reproduced by means of the double heterodyne system. Since in current VCRs the accuracy of the ordinary sync edge detection is no less than 50 ns (peak-to-peak value), supposing the SNR of the reproduced video signal is 40 dB (Vpp/Vrms), it is difficult to increase the accuracy to less than 30 ns even if using cancellation techniques for the noise superposed on the sync pulse's leading edge by 1 H delay line.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
